task.title: Materialize bounded due recurrence pages through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/927 by exposing atomic bounded due-page occurrence and task materialization through a deterministic writable CLI adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Validate recurrence identity, u64 inputs, page size 1 through 1024, and every caller-owned task identity before writable storage access.
Delegate task count, uniqueness, selection, and all-or-nothing writes to the kernel and emit ordered bindings with next_offset.
Emit one stable escaped diagnostic with nonzero status and no partial stdout or durable prefix on every failure.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused CLI integration test failed because materialize-due was an unrecognized recurrence subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added CLI tests for ordered success, empty and finite pages, maximum instants, input validation, shape errors, collisions, corruption, and rollback before dispatch existed.

attempts.diagnostic: Added parsing, validation, dispatch, kernel delegation, and deterministic materialized-page serialization; the complete workspace gate included 95 CLI integration tests.
attempts.patch: Implemented recurrence materialize-due in crates/vela-dev/src/lib.rs and documented its caller-owned cutoff and task vector boundary in ADR-0067.

attempts.summary: Recovered from false-green rate limits and applied substantive review.
attempts.diagnostic: The initial CodeRabbit status reported Review limit reached and was explicitly rejected as review evidence. After cooldown, a substantive review of all five changed files found that the maximum-instant success case did not prove empty stderr or durable max-0 and max-1 task bindings. Commit d1d30b3 added those assertions. The incremental status was again rate limited and merge remained disabled; after its cooldown, an exact-head incremental run completed with no new comments and zero unresolved threads, while marking its sole selected test file as skipped because it was similar to previously reviewed code.
attempts.patch: Strengthened the maximum-boundary test, reopened storage to verify both persisted task bindings, reran targeted and complete gates, and merged only after exact head d1d30b3ce91145640fa4fce35fdd55dd7d256420 completed the exact-head incremental check with its limited scope recorded explicitly.

outcome.summary: Operators can atomically materialize one bounded due page using explicit cutoff and task identities, with false-green review statuses excluded from merge evidence.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0193-atomic-due-recurrence-materialization-cli.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 193 records: 193 valid, 0 invalid
Pull request 928 exact head d1d30b3ce91145640fa4fce35fdd55dd7d256420 squash merge c192a4b9ac0a83eef26edab2da3aff8f18973683

lessons: A successful CodeRabbit status is false-green evidence when its comment says the review limit was reached.
After a review fix, the exact new head still needs a completed incremental review; auto-merge must remain disabled through any second cooldown.
Boundary success tests should verify stderr and reopened durable bindings, not only stdout projection.
Caller-owned cutoff and ordered task identities keep clock policy and identity allocation outside the CLI and kernel.
The command grants no claim, lease, dispatch, retry, workflow, provider, tool, permission, or execution authority.
